class.name: ProjectilePool
class.brief_description: A pooled simulator that owns every projectile in the scene.
class.description: One node simulates every projectile; none of them is a node. Projectiles live in a fixed-capacity pool and are addressed by opaque [int] handles rather than by object reference, so a handle held across frames can never address a projectile that has since ended. Motion is integrated with Velocity Verlet. Collision is a ray along the swept segment, so a projectile cannot tunnel through anything however fast it is going - the ray covers the whole step. Steps are only subdivided when they need to be: once because a curved path's chord would otherwise cut the corner by more than the projectile is wide, and once per collision, so a projectile that pierces something a third of the way through a tick spends the rest of that tick instead of stopping inside it. On collision, behaviors resolve in Path of Exile's order - Split, Pierce, Fork, Chain, Return, then Bounce - and exactly one fires per hit. A behavior that cannot be performed (a chain with nothing in range) falls through to the next rather than ending the projectile. See [ProjectileKind]. Hits are reported once per physics tick as packed arrays through [signal projectiles_hit], not once per hit: at a few hundred projectiles the per-call cost of crossing into GDScript exceeds the cost of the simulation itself. [b]This node does not draw anything.[/b] Assign a [MultiMesh] to [member multimesh] to have it write instance transforms (parent the [MultiMeshInstance3D] to this node at identity - transforms are written in this node's local space), or read [method get_positions] and drive any other renderer.

method.name: clear
method.description: Ends every projectile in flight and invalidates every outstanding handle.

method.name: clear_homing_target
method.description: Stops the projectile homing. It keeps its current velocity.

method.name: despawn
method.description: Ends one projectile. Does nothing if the handle is stale, so callers holding handles across frames need no separate liveness check.

method.name: get_live_count
method.description: How many projectiles are currently in flight.

method.name: get_positions
method.description: Every live projectile's world position, packed. Ordering is not stable across ticks - a projectile ending swap-removes the last one into its place - so this is for feeding a renderer, not for tracking an individual projectile.

method.name: get_projectile_position
method.description: World position of one projectile. Errors and returns [constant Vector3.ZERO] if the handle is stale.

method.name: get_projectile_velocity
method.description: Velocity of one projectile, in meters per second.

method.name: is_alive
method.description: Whether the handle still addresses a live projectile. Always [code]false[/code] for [code]0[/code].

method.name: set_homing_target
method.description: Points the projectile at a world position. Has no effect unless its [ProjectileKind] sets [member ProjectileKind.homing_acceleration] above zero. The target is a position, not a node: a homing projectile that outlives its target keeps its last known aim rather than dereferencing a freed object.

method.name: set_projectile_velocity
method.description: Overrides one projectile's velocity - a deflect, a gust, a time-stop release.

method.name: spawn
method.description: Adds one projectile and returns its handle, or [code]0[/code] if the pool is full. A full pool refuses rather than growing: reallocating mid-tick is a frame spike, and in VR a frame spike is the thing being avoided.

members.member: How many projectiles can be in flight at once. Changing this drops everything in flight, so set it once at set-up.
Gravity applied to every projectile, scaled per kind by [member ProjectileKind.gravity_scale]. Independent of the physics server's gravity so a projectile can arc in a world that does not.

Ceiling on how many times one projectile may be integrated - and therefore ray-queried - in a single tick. A projectile flying through empty air uses exactly one however fast it moves; each collision it survives costs another. This caps the worst case, so a projectile piercing a dense crowd cannot cost an unbounded number of queries in one tick.

Optional [MultiMesh] to write instance transforms into, one per live projectile, scaled to each projectile's radius. Recycled instances have their physics interpolation reset, without which a reused slot draws a one-frame streak from wherever its previous occupant died.

signal.name: projectiles_ended
signal.description: Emitted once per physics tick listing every projectile that left the pool - expired, out of range, consumed by a hit, or despawned. Handles in this array are already stale; they are for tearing down whatever was drawn for them.

signal.name: projectiles_hit
signal.description: Emitted once per physics tick with every collision that occurred, one entry per array per hit. Resolve a collider with [method @GlobalScope.instance_from_id]. A handle appearing here has not necessarily ended - a pierce or a chain hits and carries on. Check [method is_alive], or watch [signal projectiles_ended].
